a study of blood flow in the corpus lutem (CL) in patients undergoing gonadotropine-releasing hormone agonists (GnRHA) long protocol.
the regulation of blood flow in the corpus lutem and the effect of gonadotropins on blood flow in the CL.
the effect of the GnRH agonist on the luteal function and blood flow.

luteal phase blood flow is regulated primarily by LH.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
luteal support with HCG is useful in the patients undergoing GnRHa agonist long protocol.
luteal support by HCG administration or by vitamin E is useful to improve luteal blood supply and to improve the pregnancy rate in patients undergoing GnRHa-long protocol.

The main takeaway from our work is that
luteal phase blood flow in women undergoing the long protocol is impaired and this may be a cause of the luteal defect that occurs in these women.
